title: Wānaka: Twenty-Night Working Base
summary: Wānaka works because this is almost three weeks in one house, not a South Island road trip disguised as a work period. Early starts preserve long late-spring afternoons, two complete weekends create real excursion time, and the middle four-day mini-vacation uses only two leave days.

season.summary: Late November and early December bring long daylight, cool-to-mild temperatures and changeable alpine weather before the Christmas peak.
season.planningRange: Expect many daytime temperatures in the upper 60s or low 70s Fahrenheit, cooler nights, strong sun, wind and periodic rain; use the forecast rather than a rigid activity calendar.
notes: Daylight lasts well into the evening, which is the main reason working here remains rewarding.
Lake and river water stay cold even on warm days.
Mountain routes can be wet, windy, snowy at elevation or inaccessible despite pleasant weather in town.
Book before the pre-Christmas period tightens, but keep major outdoor plans flexible.

base.recommendation: Meadowstone or the quiet southern edge of central Wānaka
base.reason: This keeps the lakefront and town practical on foot or bike while offering a better chance of a family house and separate early-morning workspace. Albert Town is the value fallback if its property is materially better.
requirements: Three bedrooms or two bedrooms plus a genuinely separate office
A work room far enough from bedrooms for a 5 a.m. start
Verified fibre or high-quality fixed broadband and strong mobile backup
Heating, laundry, full kitchen and blackout curtains
Flexible cancellation around the long-haul flight connection

arrival.plan: Preserve Saturday daytime in Hong Kong, take a Saturday-night long-haul flight if the eventual schedule permits, connect through Auckland to Queenstown, then use a prearranged rental car for the drive to Wānaka.
arrival.fallback: If the 2027 schedule forces a Sunday departure and Monday arrival, protect Tuesday through Friday as the first work block rather than pretending arrival Monday will be normal.

workRhythm.plan: Work approximately 5 a.m.–1 p.m. New Zealand time. This maps to roughly 11 a.m.–7 p.m. New York or 10 a.m.–6 p.m. Chicago on the previous date and leaves a long afternoon.
Work approximately 5–9 a.m., remain reachable for true priorities, and use nearby afternoons rather than beginning a road trip.
Use Thursday and Friday as vacation days plus the weekend. Pick the actual activities from the ten-day forecast.
Return to visible full output before the Christmas break and pack gradually for the Saturday trip home.

ordinaryAfternoons: Walk or cycle the Wānaka lakefront and Outlet Track
Swim only with realistic cold-water expectations or use the community pool
Mount Iron for a compact local hike when wind and heat permit
Diamond Lake or the lower Rocky Mountain track when conditions are appropriate
Paddleboard or kayak close to shore in settled weather
Puzzling World, the library or an indoor recovery afternoon
Cook, read and leave some evenings deliberately empty

weekends.plan: Use one larger local outing and one recovery day. Rob Roy Glacier Track is the leading full-day candidate if road, ford and track conditions are good; otherwise use Diamond Lake, Rocky Mountain or a lake day.
This is part of the four-day forecast-selected mini-vacation rather than a separate commitment.

miniVacation.recommendation: Keep Wānaka as the base unless a two-night excursion clearly earns the packing cost.

rankedOptions.title: Wānaka and Mount Aspiring weather window
rankedOptions.tradeoff: Best fit for the one-base goal and easiest to rearrange around rain, wind and cloud.

rankedOptions.title: Two nights at Aoraki / Mount Cook
rankedOptions.tradeoff: A meaningful second landscape at a manageable distance, but it adds one lodging change and should be booked flexibly.

rankedOptions.title: Two nights in Te Anau for Milford Sound
rankedOptions.tradeoff: A major New Zealand experience, but the long transfer and weather exposure make it the most operationally expensive option.

miniVacation.pushback: Do not attempt Milford Sound as a day trip from Wānaka. If Milford becomes the priority, spend two nights in Te Anau and accept that the trip is briefly no longer a single-base model.

homeschool: Glaciation, alpine geology and the Southern Alps watershed
New Zealand birds, invasive species and conservation
Māori place names and Kāi Tahu history
Weather forecasting, UV, river crossings and mountain judgment
Time-zone arithmetic and the International Date Line
bookFirst: Twenty-night Wānaka house with separate early-morning workspace and verified broadband
Hong Kong → Auckland and Auckland → Queenstown itinerary
Queenstown rental car sized for luggage and the Wānaka transfer
Flexible Aoraki or Te Anau backup only if the family wants a two-night excursion
